doc: Standing, client-free decisions of the skeleton writer (Spec 48 §3.4). Everything a draft element can be asked that the framework database cannot answer: which text patterns are Site Info, which lines exist only because of the designer's brief, which structural shapes are a column label or a link list. A block named here must exist in the framework database (checked on every load by lib/skeleton-facts.mjs::decisionsProblems). Client-specific choices live in sites/<client>/build/skeleton/decisions.json, written by `skeleton.mjs decide`.

brandImageLink.reason: a link holding only one image whose address or label a brand of the registry owns is that brand's icon link, as one holding an svg is, so a run of them becomes the social icons row; a run of image links each to a different brand is no logo wall (logoGrid), while image links that all go to one brand (a grid of Instagram posts) stay one

columnLabel.reason: the first text child of a wrapper whose other children are a run of links is the column heading

inlineHeading.reason: a heading holding only inline content (words, an inline photo, a decorated word) stays the heading block at its level with its words in order; an inline image is the Inline photo format (Spec 02 FR-2-5, ``, resolved through the media map), a word underlined by a bare positioned layer the Highlight format (Spec 02 FR-2-4); the photo frame's border, radius and tilt are the snapshot's settings.custom.inlinePhoto tokens (2026-11-18 clone audit G-2). A worded child that renders as a box of its own (its computed display in boxDisplays) or declares its own type (an ownTypeProps value other than the heading's) is a separate piece, such as an eyebrow inside the heading: the heading keeps its words in order (a space where the piece's box ends) and each such piece is a handover row naming the line and type it loses (2026-11-19 review F6: refusing the heading would drop its own words and level)

inlineText.reason: an element whose own words sit beside inline phrasing children (a bold lead-in, a link inside a sentence, a price above a smaller note) is one text block holding every word in order as rich text: bold and italic children keep their format, a link its resolved address, a child in its own type or on its own line keeps its words and is a handover row naming what the rich text loses (structural.inlineHeading.ownTypeProps and boxDisplays). Built as a wrapper it held only the children and lost its own words. Only an element of words is claimed (no tag-map block, or the paragraph's: a link or button is the button block's, a quote the quote's); an element with no words of its own loses nothing as a wrapper

linkList.reason: a run of two or more bare text links, one above the next, is one list block; the same links side by side are separate links in a row
linkList.itemSlotsReason: the list block's draft element is its first link, which is also the block's own link part: the settings calibrated on that part (its underline) are read at the same link, never at the list root's default paint

briefOnlyLines.reason: a coming-soon line exists only because the designer's brief said the thing is not ready; it has no place on a live page
placeholder copy is replaced by real content, never built
a note that the draft's photographs are stand-ins exists only for the design review; the live site uses the client's own photographs

phone.reason: a typed UK phone number standing alone is the Site Info phone

email.reason: a typed email address standing alone is the Site Info email

copyright.reason: a line opening with a copyright mark (the marker business-info's own render uses)

hours.reason: a day name followed by a clock time (9:30, 9am) or "closed"

attribution.reason: a credit line for the agency that built the site

addressLinkPatterns.reason: a link to a maps host is an address link

logoImage.reason: an image whose file name, alt text or class says it is the brand mark

elements.reason: the theme prints its own skip link

rules.doc: Framework-wide verdicts that settle an element before any scoring (lib/skeleton-rules.mjs holds the mechanisms; each verdict names its rule id on the row, and the review groups rows by it). Precedence: a client decision, then these rules, then a finaliser pick or a standing element decision, then the database scoring. Every block named here is checked against the framework database on load.

coreExceptions.reason: a WooCommerce page's template copy prints the page's own content, WooCommerce's working block, where the draft's commerce region is (rules.commerceRegion)

filterRail.reason: the draft's filter rail on the shop template is the framework's working filter: WooCommerce's product filters inside the theme's #sgs-shop-filters aside, one heading and filter per group, as archive-product.html composes it and the theme's filter drawer builds its groups from (Spec 48 FR-48-61); found by structure from the catalogue's facets (lib/skeleton-filter-rail.mjs), never by words

commerceRegion.reason: the draft's commerce region on a WooCommerce page is WooCommerce's working piece, placed as an ordinary block that draws the region itself (Bean, 2026-10-26: these are SGS pages with the WooCommerce piece in them); the region is found by structure (lib/skeleton-commerce-region.mjs), never by words, and everything around it stays the draft's own blocks

basketCount.reason: the basket count the draft sets inside a heading's line (a pill after the words) is a row of the heading and the count; the draft's line carried a word space between them, so the row's gap is that space at the heading's font size at each device's read width, in em of that size (a typical word space is a quarter em), and its items are centred when the count is `vertical-align: middle`; what the draft's elements do not give is handed over by name (2026-11-25, lib/template-piece-woo-layout.mjs::countRowDecided)

checkoutEntry.reason: a checkout draft that shows no card fields or no order lines loop (wallet buttons, an empty basket) is still found from the fields the visitor types into: enough shown entry fields, one of them an email or phone field, a name, address or card autocomplete token, or two numeric fields

cart.reason: the cart page's content is WooCommerce's Cart block (site build keeps it, lib/site-build-plan.mjs::wooContentRole), which draws the order lines, the totals and the checkout button

checkout.reason: the checkout page's content is WooCommerce's Checkout block (kept by site build), which draws the payment form and the order summary

account.reason: the account page is an ordinary page (Bean, 2026-10-26; the hand-built reference shop's account page is the theme's page with WooCommerce's account output in it): its sign-in and account forms region is sgs/account, WooCommerce's account piece, which draws the forms, the menu and the dashboard

shop.reason: WooCommerce's product collection draws the shop's products, each in the site's own sgs/product-card, as the hand-built reference shop's archive-product copy has them; its column count is the draft's cards per row at 1440

productTile.listingReason: the element whose children are all a loop's product tiles lays the cards out, so it is the layout container, as the hand-built reference shop's home page holds its best sellers in an sgs/container grid; never a block that accepts only product cards because of that (the wishlist panel draws the visitor's saved products, not these)
productTile.reason: a tile of a priced loop on a page that is not a WooCommerce page, whose words name one product of the draft catalogue (its name, with its brand when the catalogue gives one), is the site's own product card bound to that product, the card the shop's collection draws, as the hand-built reference shop's home page has its best sellers (each an sgs/product-card in wc-product mode with its productId); found by structure and by the catalogue (lib/skeleton-product-tile.mjs), never by a draft's words; a loop any tile of which names no single product stays the draft's own blocks, because a card with no product prints nothing (2026-11-21)

pictureTileGrid.reason: a loop of titled picture tiles, each one link or control, whose parent holds only the tiles, is one card grid whose cards are the tiles (the hand-built reference shop's home page has its shape tiles as an sgs/card-grid in its overlay style, each card its picture, title and link); found by structure (lib/skeleton-picture-tiles.mjs), never by a draft's words: no price (a priced tile is a product card, rules.productTile), at most maxTileWords words a tile (a review or a description is no title), at least pictureShare of the tiles painting a picture; the style is overlay when the picture sits out of flow under the title and the default card style when it sits beside it; the block draws the cards, so the tiles' elements are absorbed and Fill writes the draft's loop into the items (2026-11-21)
pictureTileGrid.linkHandover: its link: the draft's click goes somewhere by script and names no address, so the card's link is left empty; set it to the page or the shop filter the card opens
pictureTileGrid.boundLinkHandover: its link: the draft binds each card's address to the loop's own data (a script value), so Fill writes it where the data names a page of the site and leaves the card's link empty where it does not; check where each card opens
pictureTileGrid.glyphHandover: the cards draw an inline SVG glyph: upload each card's glyph as its glyph image (glyphImage)

textTileGrid.reason: a loop of three or more whole-link tiles, each showing two lines of text (a title over a subtitle) and no picture, glyph, price or second control, whose parent holds only the tiles, is one card grid whose cards are the tiles, as the framework's brands panel holds its brand tiles and as the hand-built reference site's first brands menu did (one sgs/card-grid of twelve cards, text only): twelve cards are one items list instead of thirty-six blocks, each tile's look written once; found by structure (lib/skeleton-picture-tiles.mjs, text mode), never by a draft's words; a run of one-line links is a link list (structural.linkList) and a tile of three lines or more is a container of its own; a card whose link the draft gives no address for is a named handover (Bean, 2026-11-25)
textTileGrid.linkHandover: its link: the draft's click goes somewhere by script and names no address, so the card's link is left empty; set it to the page or the shop filter the card opens
textTileGrid.boundLinkHandover: its link: the draft binds each card's address to the loop's own data (a script value), so Fill writes it where the data names a page of the site and leaves the card's link empty where it does not; check where each card opens

messagingLink.reason: a link to a messaging app is that app's button block when it holds the app's mark and its words, a text link reading the app's Site Info address when it holds words alone (the hand-built reference sites: their WhatsApp buttons in a home page and in two footers are sgs/whatsapp-cta, inline in the page and floating where fixed to the corner; a help menu's WhatsApp text link is sgs/button with linkSource whatsapp; a WhatsApp icon alone in a social row stays the social icon); one rule over this app table, so another app is another row; found by the link's address and what it holds (lib/skeleton-messaging-link.mjs), never by its words: fixed to the viewport at every width it shows is the floating style (a label shown only from some width up hidden below it), a title over a line the card style, otherwise the inline style; the number is the site's Site Info address, which the block falls back to, named as a handover; a message the address carries is the block's message, and an address with none opens an empty chat (2026-11-21)

reviewPlatform.reason: a review section that names a review platform is that platform's review block (Bean, 2026-11-21: the Google mark, an overall rating with a review count and see-all or write-a-review links to Google make Google's reviews block, and the rule works for other platforms such as Trustpilot); one rule over this platform table, so another platform is another row; found by structure (lib/skeleton-review-platform.mjs): a loop of reviews in a section whose mark, short words or links name exactly one platform. The block keeps its default source, which shows the reviews the route writes from the draft's loop (Google: dataSource auto shows written reviews before any live ones; Trustpilot: dataSource inline), so the section always renders the draft's reviews; a live source (a Google place ID with an API key, a Trustpilot business unit) is the handover. Reviews in the client's own style stay the testimonial slider (rules.slider): those that name no platform, and those that name or link one without showing its mark (needs: the owner's own review cards with a platform's name after each date are a testimonial slider, the section showing the platform's mark is its block)

handover.detail: the reviews are the draft's, written into the block; for Google's live reviews set the block's place ID (placeId) with the site's Google API key
the reviews are the draft's, written into the block; for Trustpilot's live reviews set the block's business unit address (businessUnitUrl) and switch its source to synced

drawsChildren.reason: a block that draws the draft element's children itself, though it is neither a leaf nor holds an array item schema: the children are absorbed, never built

blocks.reason: reads its content from Site Info
draws its items, labels and carets from a WordPress menu
draws its items, numbers and carets from a WordPress menu

surfaceRoot.reason: a surface root whose kind names its block: a menu panel is the mega panel, a drawer is the navigation drawer

entries.reason: a menu surface (the panel a navigation item opens) is sgs/mega-panel
a drawer surface is sgs/nav-drawer, whose own settings draw its top row, logo, close button and body

headerSlots.columnsReason: a main bar merged from width alternatives keeps the widest bar's grid; at each other bar's widths the row lays out that bar's children, so the row's column count per device is the count of the bar shown there when its children sit side by side (the row block's default drops to one column on mobile)
headerSlots.scope: the header block always holds exactly three row blocks, top, middle and bottom; the draft's main bar (the bar holding the navigation or the logo or home link) is the middle row; a strip drawn above or below the main bar is the top or bottom row: either a sibling of the header's root that is in flow (a declared position other than fixed or absolute), renders, shares its template parent, is stacked wholly above or below the root's box at every width where both render, is not and holds at any depth no root of another surface (a surface of kind global does not count) and is adjacent to it with only out-of-flow or non-rendering siblings between (an export with no surface for the page reads a plain stacked block as a strip, listed for review), or a direct child of the header root that holds neither navigation nor logo, renders, is in flow and is stacked wholly above or below the main bar at every width where both render (a child inline with the bar is part of it); width alternatives that each hold the navigation or logo are all the main bar; the nearer of two strips on one side is the row and the other is listed, never a fourth row
headerSlots.confirm: Bean, 2026-10-22: sgs/site-header always holds exactly three sgs/site-header-row blocks (top, middle, bottom); nothing sits outside the header in an sgs_header post
headerSlots.reason: a header is always three rows: the main bar is the middle row and a strip above or below it (a top bar, an announcement or utility strip) is the top or bottom row, whether the draft draws it inside the header or beside it (Bean, 2026-10-22)

footerSlots.stackedRowReason: the row block's default lays its children out as a grid of columns; a row whose element gives it no layout and whose children the draft stacks (no two in-flow children side by side) is a one-column grid, each child full width as the draft's block flow draws them; these are structural settings only (a skeleton carries no style value, R-47-10), so the gap between the children is Fill's
footerSlots.scope: the footer block always holds exactly three row blocks, top, columns and bottom; the columns row is the footer's grid of link groups: an in-flow direct child of the footer root whose own children include two or more link groups (an element holding a link and a heading, a list, or two links) side by side at desktop, or with no such child the root's own side-by-side link groups, or with neither the in-flow child that holds such a grid deeper down (a painted band around a width wrapper: the band is the row, so its paint is the row's); the rest of the root's in-flow direct children are stacked wholly above it at every width where both render (the top row's content), wholly below it (the bottom row's) or inline with it (part of the columns); more than one on a side all go inside that row in document order, a single one is the row; a row whose own element gives it no layout and whose children the draft stacks takes stackedRow; with no column grid at any depth there is no signal where the body ends and a strip begins, so every in-flow child is in the columns row and top and bottom are empty; a floating element (declared or computed position fixed or absolute: a chat button, a back-to-top control, a global modal surface) that is a direct child of the footer root, or a sibling read beside it that holds no other surface's root, goes in the bottom row after the bottom strips and its surface is absorbed into the footer; an empty row is still emitted
footerSlots.confirm: Bean, 2026-10-22: sgs/site-footer always holds exactly three sgs/site-footer-row blocks (top, columns, bottom); nothing sits outside the footer
footerSlots.reason: a footer is always three rows: its grid of link groups is the columns row, a strip above it is the top row, a strip below it (a legal line, a copyright bar) and any floating element it carries is the bottom row (Bean, 2026-10-22)

readingProgress.reason: a full-width bar a few pixels tall, fixed to the viewport, is the Floating UI reading progress setting, not a block
readingProgress.handover: Floating UI reading progress bar: its height and its colour or gradient (shared gradient picker) are site settings

fillBar.reason: a fill bar (a bare element in the flow, alone in a parent that declares its own height, filling that height and a percentage of its width with a fill: a rating breakdown's bar, a progress meter) sits at its parent's start corner, so as a layer its top and left edges are 0

decorationLayer.reason: a bare layer that only paints a fill, gradient, glow or bar is a decorative image at its own position, size, radius and fill (Bean, 2026-11-07)

overlayLayer.coverSlotsReason: the calibrated slots that cover their block's whole box: the shared background renderer (plugins/sgs-blocks/includes/media/render-background.php, includes/media/background-css.php::sgs_bg_overlay_css) prints the overlay as a direct child of the block's root, placed at inset 0, painted by `.uid > .sgs-bg-overlay`
overlayLayer.reason: a bare layer that paints only a gradient or a fill and covers its host block's whole box, above the host's background and below its content, is the host's own overlay when the host block has one: its look is absorbed by its parent, never made a block of its own (Bean, 2026-11-21); several such layers stack into the one setting with the layer drawn last on top

backgroundPicture.reason: an empty element marked role="img" that paints a picture as its background is a media block: the picture and its alt are read from it, never dropped as an unplaced element

kinds.reason: a layer whose gradient follows the pointer (a --gx / --gy custom property) is the motion glare layer, not a block
kinds.detail: pointer glare: the block's Glare effect (sgs-motion-layer, fx-glare.css) paints it; set the effect on the block this layer sits in

kinds.reason: a layer the draft's code fills with a loaded animation file is the hero's animated SVG setting, not a block
kinds.detail: hero animated SVG: the hero block draws it from its animated-background settings

kinds.reason: a line the draft draws in as it enters is the owning block's connector setting, not a block
kinds.detail: drawn line: the block that owns the steps or timeline draws its connector (its connector settings)

decorativeShape.reason: a floating shape that draws an outline (a ring) is a decorative image

typedDivider.reason: a typed divider between items is the row's separators setting, not a block

homeLink.linkSlotsReason: the draft sizes a logo by the link round it (a declared width, a ceiling and centring on the link, the image 100% of it); the logo block draws its own link, so the dissolved link is read at the link part's calibrated slot of the width setting (lib/skeleton-wrapper-link-slot.mjs), which reads only the looks of the settings calibrated there (the width) and a look the part paints by default at the link's value (no underline). A ceiling or centring on the link is calibrated at the logo's root, not its link part, so such a link stays a node (Bean, 2026-11-21: a wrapper's CSS is never dropped). A link round several logos, or a block the calibration has no such slot for, is read for none
homeLink.reason: the link around a logo goes: the logo block links home itself. A link around two or more logos (a mark and a wordmark) is kept as a plain container holding them, so the pair stays one item of the row it sits in (a grid or flex row places one cell for it) and keeps the link's own gap and alignment

widthWrapper.reason: a centring width wrapper (max-width with auto margins) inside a header, footer, row or section block goes: that block sets its own width; its children take its place, and the wrapper is the draft element of the calibrated slot of the block's hostSetting, so its width, layout and gaps are read there

numberedSteps.reason: a parent whose children are all steps, each typing its own number (1, 2, 3 or 01, 02, 03) beside its words with the numbers counting up from 1, is one process-steps block holding each step's number, title and description (the hand-built reference sites build their numbered steps as sgs/process-steps: a stacked list in its list layout, a row of steps in its row layout; none builds them as a numbered icon list, and a row of numbered cards that paint their own box, such as four reasons on dark tiles, is built as containers). Found by structure (lib/skeleton-numbered-steps.mjs), never by words: no step holds a control, a picture or a painted box of its own (cardPaint), at most three pieces of text a step, the title at most maxTitleWords words, and a step explains (a description, or a title of at least minTitleWords words: a number beside a short label is a contents list, the list block's numbered marker); a number the draft never types (a counter or a CSS marker) stays the list block's marker, and a run whose numbers are not 1..n (years, a word) is a timeline and is not claimed (2026-11-22)

listHeading.reason: the first piece of text of a footer column, directly above a run of text links, is that list's own heading (sgs/icon-list holds heading and headingLevel; the hand-built reference shop's footer menus are each one icon list with its heading, level p where the draft's heading is no h tag): one block instead of a heading block and a list block, and the heading's look is read at the list's heading part

listWrapper.reason: a bare wrapper whose only content is one list goes: the list block is that wrapper

backToTop.reason: a back-to-top control is a link whose source is 'top' (the shared link source): a container whose whole box is the link when it holds a label and an icon, a button when it is words alone; a control is one by its words, its handler's name, or what its handler does (it scrolls the page to its top and writes no state: lib/skeleton-scroll-top.mjs, 2026-11-21)

floating.reason: a back-to-top control fixed to the viewport at every width it shows is the Floating UI panel's back to top, a site option that draws its own button, so the control places no block (2026-11-21)
floating.handover: Floating UI back to top: switch it on in the site options (sgs_floating_ui_back_to_top_enabled), with its corner (sgs_floating_ui_back_to_top_position) and its colours (sgs_floating_ui_back_to_top_bg_colour, sgs_floating_ui_back_to_top_icon_colour)

mapEmbed.reason: an embedded map is sgs/business-info's map display
mapEmbed.handover: map source: the Google Business Profile listing when Site Info has one (preferred), else the address

openStatus.reason: a live open or closed line (text the draft's code computes from the clock against the opening hours it holds, lib/skeleton-clock.mjs) is sgs/business-info's open-status display, computed in the visitor's browser from the Site Info hours

timeText.reason: text the draft's code picks by the hour of the clock (a conditional chain on getHours, lib/skeleton-clock.mjs) is the text block's time-based text option: one hour range per branch with its words, swapped in the visitor's browser

hoursRows.reason: a day and its opening times laid out as a row is sgs/business-info's hours display (rows layout); the day and time columns are drawn by it

drawerOpener.reason: a button or link whose click handler opens a surface of kind drawer is the burger the header's navigation block draws itself below its collapse point, so the navigation block takes it; the handler opens the drawer when it writes a state key (a toggle included) that one of the drawer's surfaces.json states holds at true (lib/skeleton-handler-opens.mjs), or when the drawer's opened_by words name it; a control opening a drawer the page map hands to a block is that block first (rules.blockPartOpener)

drawerClose.scope: a button with no letter or digit in its words, on a drawer surface, whose click handler writes a closing value (a falsy literal) to a state key one of the record's drawer surfaces holds at true when open
drawerClose.reason: the drawer block draws its own close button, so the draft's close button is the drawer's close part: absorbed into the drawer root, its look read at the close part's calibrated slot (lib/skeleton-part-slots.mjs::partSlots); a worded button or link that also shuts the drawer (a menu link) stays its own block

pillButton.reason: a link or button holding exactly one label (and a glyph) is one button whose glyph is its own icon; a toggle, a slider arrow and a link with no words are not pills; a lone link is a button too, which can be styled as a plain link

wholeCardLink.reason: a link holding two or more pieces of text, or a heading, is a container whose whole box is the link, a call to action that ends it being the card's button drawn as a cue with no link (cardAction); a link that paints a picture itself and holds one label is a picture tile, a container whose whole box is the link, with the label a badge block inside it

siteInfoLink.reason: a lone link to a phone number, an email address or a maps host is a button whose link reads Site Info (no typed tel: or mailto:), with its label from Site Info when the words are the value itself

linkSourceForKind.reason: the shared link source each Site Info kind becomes on a link

briefOnlyEntry.reason: a menu entry with no link that says it is coming soon (a lone badge word such as SOON beside its label, or the words themselves) exists only because the designer's brief said the page is not ready: there is no point putting a coming-soon item in a link list (Bean, 2026-10-09), so the entry is dropped from the menu, listed for removal, and never built as a disabled item

navigation.reason: the navigation inside a header is the menu bar block and inside a drawer the drawer menu block; both draw their items from a WordPress menu

splitMenu.scope: a link or button of a header, outside every nav element, whose words are the label of an item the page map flagged `splitItem` in the main header menu (lib/skeleton-split-menu.mjs, from lib/intake-pagemap-split.mjs), and the header's nav itself
splitMenu.reason: the navigation links on the logo's far side from the header's nav are items of the nav's own menu, so the menu is drawn twice: the nav as its first half and the far side's links as one menu bar bound to the same menu, with splitSide and the item the split falls after on both, and no burger on the far side's (the nav owns the drawer's). The far side's first link is that bar; the others are its items. Each half reads its own gap and padding: the far side's bar at the group holding its links, its items at its first link (Spec 48 FR-48-30)

megaOpenerMenu.scope: a link or button of a header, outside every nav element, whose words are the label of an item the page map flagged `megaOpener` in a second header menu (lib/skeleton-mega-opener.mjs, from lib/intake-pagemap-mega-slots.mjs::megaSlots)
megaOpenerMenu.reason: a header control outside the nav that opens a mega panel is an item of the second header menu, so it is a menu bar bound to that menu (the main menu owns the drawer's burger) and the item and its panel are one thing (Spec 48 FR-48-30)

glyphDisc.reason: a typed glyph (a tick, a star, an arrow, a currency sign) alone in a painted round box of equal width and height, outside any link or button but a whole-card link, is a disc the draft draws: sgs/icon with the glyph as its emoji character; the box is judged at the widest width it renders (a flex row can squeeze it narrower at a phone width), and a disc inside a link that holds two or more other pieces of text or a heading is part of that card, while a glyph that is a link's only content (an arrow link) is no disc; a plus, minus, cross or opening quote is a control or a quotation, never a disc

solitaryIcon.reason: a glyph on its own (any icon library, an emoji alone, or a glyph the draft injects from a script value) is sgs/icon, an emoji or typed glyph as the icon's emoji character (never its brand name); an emoji inside running text stays typed in the text

leadingDot.reason: a dot that leads a label's words (its only child, a round marker with a fill of its own at the start of its content) is the label's own dot, so the dot setting is on and the dot's look is read at the label's dot layer; a line of words led by such a dot, on one line and alone among its siblings, is a label whatever its length or case (stacked rows of a dot and words stay one list, Bean 2026-10-19)

label.reason: a short run of words set in capitals, wide tracking or a pill is a kicker, eyebrow or pill, and a single line led by a dot is a status label: sgs/label; never a control the visitor operates (a button, a click handler, a pressed or expanded state) and never a bare number

clientBuiltSurface.reason: a surface the client already built as a post (a header, drawer or mega menu) follows that post's block tree

logoElement.reason: a custom element named as a logo (its tag matches logoImage, such as <brand-logo>) is the logo block, which reads the site logo

columnHeading.reason: the first piece of text in a column that sits directly in a header or footer row heads that column (sgs/heading), whatever its type style

mediaElement.reason: a custom element the draft uses as an image placeholder (<image-slot>) is sgs/media

logoGrid.reason: a group of three or more links that each hold only an image (a logo wall) is sgs/gallery with a link per image; the links are its items
logoGrid.itemSlotsReason: the tiles' look (border, radius, background, padding) is the block's tile settings, calibrated on its first item: the draft's first link is read there

cardTitle.reason: the first plain piece of text in a whole-card link titles the card (sgs/heading); text set as a kicker stays a label

wrappedWords.reason: an element's own words in a block that holds its body as inner blocks (it wraps a container, as sgs/quote) are one body child of this block, read at the same draft element; the block's first text setting names another part (the quote's attribution) and its empty body prints the editor placeholder

listArrangement.scope: a listed block that draws its items from the draft's repeated units (the draft element's block children) whose units sit in one row at the widest width they render at (each starts at or beyond the previous one's right edge, and each overlaps the first unit's height; lib/skeleton-arrangement.mjs::inOneRow). The block's own setting takes the listed value; a decision's own value for the setting wins, and units stacked or wrapped onto a second row keep the block's default. A row of equal columns (each unit's width within a pixel of the first's) also takes the entry's `equalShare` setting
listArrangement.reason: a timeline whose entries the draft sets side by side in one row is the timeline's horizontal orientation, where the block's default draws them down the page (four year entries along a line, each with a title and a line of words beneath)

itemFieldSlots.scope: a listed block that draws its entries from a loop of the draft: the draft element of the loop's first copy that prints the entry's field (the field the list pass puts into the part's item key, a draft `year` into the timeline's `date`) is where the settings of the part's css_elements are read, at the slot calibration measured them at (lib/skeleton-item-field-slots.mjs). An element printing two fields, or no calibrated slot for the part's settings, gives no slot and a note on the row. A block's `list` names the css_elements of the part that holds the entries (a timeline's card row): the draft element that lays out the loop's copies is where their settings (the gap between cards) are read, at the slot calibration measured them at
itemFieldSlots.reason: a timeline's year ring is the element that prints the entry's date: its size, border, fill, radius, shadow and padding are the block's year-ring settings, and its type the date settings, read at the draft's own ring and not at the timeline's root, where they paint nothing; the entry's title and its description are parts of the same kind (their colour, size and weight settings are read at the draft's own title and description, not at the root, which none of them paint)

marquee.itemSlotsReason: the name tiles' look (fill, radius, shadow, padding, border) is the block's tile settings, calibrated on its first text tile: the draft's first labelled tile is read there

textItems.handover: each brand's link: the draft opens the shop filtered by that brand; set each brand's link, or switch the strip's source to the shop's product brands
textItems.reason: a looping strip of links each naming a brand in words (no picture) is the brand strip showing names (brandDisplay text, in one row), its links' words the brands, a loop doubled for the scroll read once; read wherever it sits, so a brand strip inside its own section is still one

tile.reason: a labelled tile the draft paints itself (an inline background, border or box shadow) is a name tile: the strip draws each name as a tile (brandTextTile) in the tile layout (logoLayout tiles; the row layout draws no tile, and the rule owns the setting so Fill never answers it from a lone max-width read), and the first tile's look is read at the block's tile settings (itemSlots) where the block's default shows the names bare

tileSize.reason: a strip of square tiles the draft sizes in pixels per device (150, 136 and 112) is the logo block's count of tiles per device (columns) and its tile cap per device (maxHeight, maxHeightTablet, maxHeightMobile): the block shares the strip's width among the count and never draws a tile larger than that device's cap, and a length per device is no setting it holds. Each device's cap is the draft's tile at that device (a device whose cap is what the cascade already gives writes none) and its count the most tiles that still leave each one at least that size, so the cap draws the tile and it is the draft's size to the pixel

labelledLogos.reason: a looping strip of logo tiles that each name themselves (an aria-label) shows each name where its picture is not set yet and the picture once it is, so a strip of empty picture placeholders presents its brands by name and never as an empty band; Fill writes each tile's label as the item's name (lib/fill-list-items.mjs::holeField)

marquee.reason: a strip whose own animation loops a translate for ever (the motion inventory's record, never a name) is a marquee: logos make sgs/brand-strip, labels make sgs/trust-bar, and the repeated items are its items; the route writes no marquee motion until M7

trustBar.reason: a trust bar is a section block (block_composition.container_kind section): a page's own section that is a row of short non-interactive labels side by side, each with at most a glyph, at least one naming a capability the framework database records for sgs/trust-bar (accreditation, certification, halal), is sgs/trust-bar with the labels as its items; the same badges inside a section are sgs/label blocks in a row (Bean, 2026-10-13). The ignored capabilities (collection, features, icons) describe the block, not what its badges say

loneLabel.reason: a lone label whose glyph comes before its words, in a header (a header surface, or a template's own header element), outside any link or button, is a trust bar of one item: the glyph is the item's icon, drawn bare, and the words its label; a label that reads differently at other widths is noted for the content page

headerStripBar.reason: a run of two or more labels side by side in a strip above or below a header's main bar (its top or bottom row), each a short line of words that is no link, button, heading, number or business detail and draws at most a glyph beside its words, is one sgs/trust-bar inside that row: each label is an item, its glyph the item's icon (the rendered SVG, a loop doubled for its scroll read once), the icons drawn bare as the draft draws them (at the size its SVGs state on their root, when every label states the same one: `style.iconSize`) or the words alone when no label has one, and the first label is where Fill reads the items' spacing and type. A header strip is no page section, so the trust bar's section rule (trustBar) and its marquee rule never place it there; a glyph with no letter between two labels is their separator, never an item

splitMedia.reason: a hero's split picture fills a column of the hero: a picture narrower than 64px or a tenth of the hero's width at the widest width it renders (an icon in an advice card, a thumbnail) is no split media, and neither is a picture inside a link or button that holds more than the picture (a control's own mark: the picture fills less than half of the control's box at the widest width it renders); a picture that is most of its link (a wide hero image wrapped in an address) is still the split media; a hero with no such picture is the plain hero

hero.reason: the first section of a page holding its h1 is sgs/hero (its label, heading, text and buttons are its content; an image inside makes it the split hero); a hero whose content block the draft places absolutely against the hero's bottom or top edge takes that side as its vertical alignment (verticalAlignment: the setting's value for each side; lib/skeleton-hero-background.mjs::contentAnchor); a split hero's order at each device is the draft's: its picture before or after its words where the draft draws them at that device's width (splitOrder: the value the setting takes per device for each order; desktop's empty value is the content column first); its picture's alignment in its column is the draft's declared justify-self, or centred under auto side margins (splitAlignment: the setting's value for each CSS keyword)

frame.reason: the wrapper that frames the hero's picture (a border, rounded corners, a shadow, a clip or a set ratio around an image placeholder) is the draft element of the split-media part's calibrated slot, so its look is read there; the picture inside it is the media itself, which draws no frame of its own

heroInner.reason: inside a hero, its image is the hero's own split media and its layout wrappers go (the hero lays out its content and media columns); a wrapper laying items side by side (a button group, a row of labels) stays; the wrapper stacking two or more items with no picture inside is the hero's content column, the draft element of contentSetting's calibrated slot

heroCollage.reason: a positioned wrapper inside a hero whose absolutely placed children include two or more that hold a picture (a pile of tilted photo frames, a sticker, a tag) is a collage: the hero's split media holds one picture, so the wrapper stays a container that sets the layers' space and the hero stays a standard hero (lib/skeleton-hero-collage.mjs)

heroCollageLayer.reason: each absolutely placed child of a hero's collage wrapper is a decorative image layer at its own position, size, rotation and order, holding what the draft puts in it (the photo and its caption); a hero with one picture beside its content has no collage and stays a split hero

heroCollageRow.reason: a hero's own layout holds one split media, so a hero whose collage stage sits beside its words keeps the wrapper that lays them side by side, and the column of words beside the stage, as containers: they are the grid the hero does not draw (lib/skeleton-hero-collage.mjs)

heroBackdrop.reason: a picture the draft lays behind the hero's content (an absolutely placed layer covering the hero's whole box, with no words of its own) is the hero's background picture, read at the hero's background setting; the hero stays a full-width hero and no split media part is read from it (lib/skeleton-hero-background.mjs::behindContent)

marqueeFrame.reason: the frame that only clips or fades a marquee track goes: sgs/brand-strip draws its own overflow, and a masked edge fade belongs to its marquee motion (Bean, 2026-10-13)

mountWrapper.reason: a mounted component's wrapper (the host element the runtime stamps for a dc-import, or the component's own root inside it) that holds one child, no words and no declared style but display, leads down to one control (a link, button or field: `controls`), and draws the same box as that child at every read width, goes: it sizes, places and paints nothing, so a button or field built once and mounted (Spec 48A FR-48A-17) is the block it would be if drawn where it stands (2026-11-19)

alignWrapper.reason: a wrapper whose only declared styles align or space its content (text alignment, padding, margin) goes where nothing is lost, and its CSS is never dropped (Bean, 2026-11-21, correcting the reading of his 2026-10-13 ruling that side padding goes with the wrapper, which he calls misconstrued): centred text is read at the nodes inside; a wrapper that is its parent's only content and pads, caps or lays out only as the parent block's settings can is absorbed by the parent, its values read at the part those settings paint and its padding summed with the parent's per side (lib/skeleton-absorb-wrapper.mjs, lib/fill-absorbed.mjs); any other padding or width no reader takes keeps the wrapper as a node (paint conservation, lib/skeleton-rules.mjs::ruleFor's unwrap guard, Bean 2026-11-20); anything that paints, positions or lays out stays (Bean, 2026-10-13)

siblingGap.scope: a wrapper that follows a sibling in its parent and declares a margin: the margin is the gap between the two blocks, not spacing inside the wrapper
siblingGap.reason: unwrapping a wrapper that declares a margin against its previous sibling would lose the gap between the two blocks, so the wrapper stays (Bean approved the mega aside's text column as sgs/container, 2026-10-21)

blockPadding.scope: a wrapper that declares padding above or below its content (a page section's padding around its centred column)
blockPadding.reason: the space a wrapper's top and bottom padding make is never lost (Bean, 2026-10-28, Spec 48 FR-48-101; Bean, 2026-11-21: a wrapper's CSS is never dropped): the wrapper goes only where its parent absorbs it (it is the parent's only content and the parent block's part holds its padding, summed with the parent's own per side: lib/skeleton-absorb-wrapper.mjs, lib/fill-absorbed.mjs); otherwise it stays and carries its own padding. The unwrap guard (paint conservation) keeps any other padded wrapper too, side padding included, and this entry still decides a wrapper the guard lets through (a hero picture's frame); alignment alone still goes with the wrapper

cardAction.typedArrowReason: an arrow typed as a character in a box of its own after the words of a call to action (the hand-built reference shop's "Shop gifts" with its arrow in a filled circle is an sgs/button with icon arrow-right and an icon background) is that button's icon, not a text leaf: the call to action is the element holding the words, the arrow leaf is absorbed into it as its icon part, and the card's link goes on the button (a card whose last text leaf was the arrow had no action, so its link was dropped)
cardAction.boundLinkReason: a card whose address is a script value (the order's view page) keeps its link on the button for now: the later order stage (lib/template-piece-order.mjs) binds a link on the block inside a card whose own block takes no bound address, and it does not yet set the card's link source (sgsBlockLinkSource 'order-view', already in the plugin), so a card link here would be a fixed address and the bound button a dead cue
cardAction.reason: a card the draft draws as one link (its anchor wraps the whole card) is one whole-card link, whether or not a short call to action (a glyph beside it, or below two other pieces of text) ends it (Bean, 2026-11-22: it is completely dependent on what the draft does); the call to action is the card's button drawn as a cue (visualOnly: a plain span, no link inside a link), its icon and look kept; a card whose draft links only its button (a div card holding one link) keeps the button as the link

formControl.reason: a form control is the SGS field block for its rendered type (a required checkbox with no other checkbox in its group is the consent field; a type with no field of its own is a text field; submit, reset and image inputs are buttons); its label, required marker and hint become that block's label, required and help text; a <label> wrapped round it goes (Bean, 2026-10-19); two or more radios or ticks of one group in a form are one radio or checkbox field holding their options, its label, marker and hint read as one field's (FR-48-57)
formControl.fieldTextReason: the field's label, required marker, hint or character count: the field block's own label, required and help text settings draw it (Bean, 2026-10-19)

fieldIcon.reason: the mark drawn inside a text field's own box (a magnifier at the start of a search field) is the field block's leadingIcon setting, drawn after the Lucide icon it copies; the field block draws it, so the mark goes

wrapperCap.reason: a <label> round a control that holds no words and renders as the control's own box is the field itself, so the cap the draft declares on it (a search box narrower than its row) is the field block's own maxWidth setting for the desktop tier; the control's computed max-width is none, so nothing else reads it

formLink.reason: a draft form on a page is the saved form post (Spec 42): the page holds the form block linked to it, with no fields of its own, and the form's fields are cloned once on the form's own surface (Bean, 2026-10-25)
formLink.droppedReason: a second element under the form's root: the form is one linked embed, so nothing else of the form stays on the page

taughtBy.key: TradeApplication/16, TradeApplication/10, TradeApplication/85 and the schema getter

formSteps.scope: a form surface whose draft logic holds a form schema of two or more steps (lib/skeleton-form-steps.mjs): the draft's step list, step count and Next / Back buttons inside the form, and the schema fields the page never rendered

reasons.indicator: the draft's list of the form's steps: the form block draws its own step list and progress bar from its steps' labels
reasons.count: the draft's step count: the form block draws its own progress (its step list numbers each step)
reasons.next: the draft's Next button: the form block draws its own Next button between steps
reasons.back: the draft's Back button: the form block draws its own Previous button between steps
reasons.progress: a wordless element beside the draft's step list or step count (its progress line): the form block draws its own progress bar

formSteps.reason: a multi-step draft form is the form block with one sgs/form-step per schema step (Spec 42, Spec 48 FR-48-57): each step holds its schema fields, those the page never rendered built from the schema by their type (an input type or tag of rules.formControl, else the draft's own type word here), and the draft's step list, step count and Next / Back buttons are the form's own progress and step navigation, never static blocks beside it (2026-10-27)

formHost.reason: a draft <form> element is the sgs/form block, whose fields sit inside it and whose field settings (border, background, padding, font) paint every field's input part

cardHeading.reason: the first piece of text in a card that is not a bare number, set bold and larger than the text after it, titles the card (sgs/heading), whether or not the card is a link (Bean, 2026-10-19)

dotMarker.reason: a small dot or short bar that holds nothing, is no control and sits beside text is the marker of the block holding the text (a label's dot, a list item's marker, the separator between a row's items); stacked rows of a marker and one piece of text are one list (Bean, 2026-10-19)

items.marksNote: the trust bar has no separator setting (a glyph and its colour drawn between items), so the separator is not built

marqueeCodeItems.itemsReason: the strip's rendered items (read by the inventory as codeItems: each item's own words and its one inline SVG, a doubled loop read once) are the trust bar's items, its words the label and its SVG the icon; the strip's words would otherwise land in the block's title, so the title is cleared. Items with no icon take the word-only badge style (`plain`); the first item's element is read for the item's spacing and the label's type (`slots`: the settings whose calibrated element is the item and its label, read at the code-built item's own element through its child-index path)
marqueeCodeItems.handover: the strip's items are built by the draft's code (its template holds one text binding): add each item to the trust bar
marqueeCodeItems.scope: an element in the motion inventory's looping keys (its own animation is an infinite translate, intake's re-derived record with the strip as nearest_tpl_id) that has no stamped children and whose template holds a text binding the logic builds
marqueeCodeItems.reason: a strip whose items are created in code and whose own animation loops a translate for ever is a marquee like one with template items: a scrolling sgs/trust-bar (Bean, 2026-10-21)

megaGroup.scope: a direct child of the root of a surface of kind menu or panel whose parent surface is a header and that something opens (its surfaces.json opened_by, or an aria-expanded control in the header); the panel's declared display is flex or grid; the child shares the free space (a declared flex-grow, or a fractional or minmax(0, ...) grid track) and holds a run of sibling links directly (a loop of links, or two or more static links with one declared style), or (`headedRun`) a heading or label (a leaf of words that is not a link) followed, at most one plain wrapper down (no words, no paint of its own, the only block child), by an element holding such a run whose links each carry words and no block of their own; a gallery of picture links, a grid of cards and a promo are not a headed run; or (`textColumn`) a stack of text alone in the panel's row: two or more block children, each a leaf of words that is not a link and holds no block, as a static column or as a loop's repeated item (a loop's item holding a picture or a link inside is not one; an inline icon is a part of the item)
megaGroup.reason: a growing child of a header's disclosure panel that holds a run of sibling links is a mega group: the panel's column of links (Bean's approved header mega menus, 2026-10-21)

megaAside.scope: the same panel as megaGroup; the child is a fixed or ratio-sized box (a declared width that does not shrink, a fixed grid track, or an aspect ratio) with paint of its own (a declared background, border or shadow, or a style-bound one) and holds no run of links; a loop's repeated card is never an aside
megaAside.reason: a fixed or ratio-sized painted box beside a header disclosure panel's links, holding no link run, is the panel's aside: its feature or call-to-action card (Bean's approved header mega menus, 2026-10-21)

megaContainer.scope: the same panel as megaGroup; the child shares the free space, is not a fixed box and is neither a run of sibling links nor a heading over a run of text links (its content is a heading and a non-link grid, or a gallery of picture links)
megaContainer.reason: a growing child of a header disclosure panel with no run of links of its own is a plain container, not a mega group (Bean approved the brands panel's heading and logo grid as sgs/container, 2026-10-21)

optionSet.scope: an element whose block children are all buttons carrying an aria-pressed or aria-checked state (read from the fact record, the render confirms), as a loop (an sc-for) or a run of two or more, and that is neither inside a form element nor narrows a list; a lone button, a run without a pressed or checked state and a disclosure button (aria-expanded) are not an option set
optionSet.reason: a group of pressable chips (sizes, flavours, any option set) is the exclusive single-select option picker, which draws its own options: the chips and their label and tick spans are absorbed into it

hideLabel.reason: the legend the picker prints above its options is its own, never a chip's: a draft's group holds only its chips, so the stray default legend is switched off and any heading the draft has above the group is built as its own block

chipSlots.reason: the chips' look (colours, border, radius, shadow, padding, type, in the resting and the selected state) is the block's pill settings, calibrated on its options: each setting is read at the draft's chip at the option position its calibrated slot names (the first chip is the one selected at rest)

optionSetForm.scope: an option set (the optionSet scope) with a form element (the real tag form) among the ancestors in its template parent chain, or on a form surface (whose root is the form block whatever its tag, rule formHost) when the group filters no list (a filtering group there stays optionSetFilter); the same group outside a form stays the option picker
optionSetForm.reason: a group of pressable chips inside a form is a choice the form submits: the tiles field, which takes its options from the chips' text (Bean, 2026-10-21)

optionSetFilter.handover: the choice narrows a list on this page: wire it to the list's filter
optionSetFilter.scope: an option set outside a form element whose chips loop a renderVals list, when the draft's logic writes a state key from those chips' handlers and filters another list an sc-for of the same component iterates by that key (lib/skeleton-narrowing.mjs, read from the logic's syntax tree); a computed state key, a list not filtered by the key and a group with static chips narrow nothing
optionSetFilter.reason: a group of pressable chips whose choice narrows a list on the same surface stays the option picker and hands the filter wiring to the site build (Bean, 2026-10-21)

categoryFilter.reason: on the shop template, a row of chips that narrows the product listing by the catalogue's categories is the shop's category filter: WooCommerce's product_cat taxonomy filter in the chips display style (built from rules.filterRail's category group and choice style), so it filters the listing; the option picker would hand the wiring to a site build that nothing carries out on the shop template (shop-5)

megaPanelRow.scope: a header disclosure panel (the same panel as megaGroup) whose root declares no grid or flex layout of its own: the first descendant reached only through plain wrappers (each the only block child of the one above, with no words and not a loop's item), at most three levels down, that lays two or more children out as a grid or flex row and has at least one child that is a mega group, aside or container (a loop's repeated card never counts); the wrappers down to and including that row are unwrapped (the first one declaring a max-width or padding records them as the panel's own maxWidth and panelPadding, when the panel's own element paints; a wrapper that paints anything of its own stays a node), and the row's children are the panel's columns, read by megaGroup, megaAside and megaContainer against the row's own tracks (an auto-fit or auto-fill repeat of a fractional track sizes every child); when the wrappers instead end in an element that lays nothing out and holds a run of links or a heading over one (`soleColumn`), that element is the panel's only column and a mega group
megaPanelRow.reason: a header disclosure panel's columns sit in a row inside width and layout wrappers (a width cap, the grid): the panel block holds the width and lays its columns out, so the wrappers go, their width, padding and layout read by the panel's own settings, and each column is a mega group, aside or container

megaGridContainer.scope: the root element of a surface of kind menu or panel whose parent surface is a header and that something opens (the same panel as megaGroup), when it declares its own grid layout and its own paint (a declared or style-bound background, border or shadow) or its own padding; a root that declares no grid, or neither paint nor padding, stays the panel shell
megaGridContainer.reason: a header disclosure panel's root that lays its own grid out and carries its own padding or paint is the container that holds the cards, not the panel shell (Bean approved the sectors panel's gradient card grid as sgs/container, 2026-10-21)

drawerIconRun.handover: the drawer's top row shows this icon group: set sgs/nav-drawer chromeSlotType to icons and keep the group the first block of the drawer body (includes/nav-drawer-chrome-icons.php lifts it into the top row)
drawerIconRun.scope: two or more consecutive icon-only links, in the top row of a surface of kind drawer (the first child of the drawer root that sits in the flow), whose targets are Site Info kinds the brand registry owns (a tel: or mailto: address, a social profile host)
drawerIconRun.reason: a run of icon-only phone, email and social links in a drawer's top row is one social icons group in the drawer's icons top-row slot, each icon linking its Site Info key (Bean's decision 1, 2026-10-21)

blockOwnedPart.scope: a surface whose root the page map holds as a part with owner `block` of another row (lib/skeleton-surface-role.mjs, the part's draftId naming the surface's record or its root's tag and aria-label); the owning block comes from the row's template

cart.reason: the cart page's bag drawer is the cart block's own drawer (sgs/cart displayMode drawer draws its heading, lines, totals, empty message and checkout button: Spec 27, FR-48-87)

blockOwnedPart.reason: a drawer the page map holds as a block-owned part of another row is drawn by that block, never the navigation drawer: the block is the surface's root and every element in it is absorbed (Bean, 2026-10-23, plan 2026-10-23-cloning-tool-completion S5: the bag drawer is part of the cart block)

ownedPart.scope: a surface's root, when the page map holds the surface as a part of another row and gives it no row of its own (lib/skeleton-surface-role.mjs::surfaceRole role ownedPart: a part naming the surface's record with owner woocommerce, page or draft-notes, or a surface other than a page, header or footer on a WooCommerce row's page, its route the row's own or one the row folds in)
ownedPart.pieceReason: the page map holds this surface as a part of a WooCommerce row, so the row's WooCommerce piece (rules.commerceRegion.roles, the role's owner block, else its block) draws it: the piece is the root and every element in it is absorbed, never cloned as its own form or blocks (Bean, 2026-10-30, FR-48-87)
ownedPart.rowReason: the page map holds this surface as a part of another row with no row of its own, so that row's own surface builds it and this surface places nothing (Bean, 2026-10-30, FR-48-87)
ownedPart.reason: a part the page map gives another row is drawn by that row: by its WooCommerce piece on a WooCommerce row, else by the row's own surface; it is never built as its own form or blocks (Bean, 2026-10-30)

blockPartOpener.selfPartReason: the control is the block's own trigger: the trigger's settings (a pill's padding, border, radius and type) are read at the control itself, and its icon, label and count at the trigger's sub-parts where the draft's children line up with them
blockPartOpener.scope: in a surface of kind header, a button or link whose click handler (a renderVals key of its component) writes a state key that a drawer's surfaces.json state holds at true, where the page map holds that drawer as a part with owner `block` of a row whose template names its owning block in rules.blockOwnedPart.byTemplate (lib/skeleton-handler-opens.mjs, lib/skeleton-surface-role.mjs::blockPartSurfaces)
blockPartOpener.reason: the control that opens a drawer the page map hands to a block is that block, which draws both the drawer and its own trigger: the control's label, count and icon become the block's trigger settings (byTemplate.<template>.trigger) and are absorbed, never a container in the header (the bag pill is sgs/cart in drawer mode with a pill trigger; Bean S5, 2026-10-23)

surfaceOpener.scope: a button or link whose click handler makes every opening write of a modal, choice flow or form row of the page map (lib/skeleton-openers.mjs, the reading of lib/intake-pagemap-openers.mjs), on any surface but the target's own
surfaceOpener.reason: a control that opens a modal, starts a flow or fills a form is a button linking the target's anchor, and the target's frame (an sgs/modal with no trigger of its own, holding the linked flow for a flow) is placed once on the surface holding it, the footer or header's frame serving every page; the draft's backdrop, panel and close control are the frame's own settings and only the dialog's inner content is the modal post (Spec 48 FR-48-95, Bean 2026-10-28)

choiceFlow.question: sgs/choice-flow-question
choiceFlow.scope: the surface the page map holds as an sgs_choice_flow row (its draftId names the surface's surfaces.json record), read from the fact record (lib/skeleton-choice-flow.mjs): a question is a loop whose item holds a button its handler binds to the loop item, its words the text in the loop's container (or the text just before it), its options the loop's recorded values; a conditional panel after a question's options is a step it opens underneath; the summary is the flow's aside; close, skip, add to bag, continue and back are buttons named by their handler or words; then two or more pressable buttons under one parent are a question whose revealing option opens what its condition shows, a live line naming two questions' picks is the summary, the one text after the last control the stage note, and every other worded element with no control a block of the flow post beside the flow (lib/skeleton-choice-flow-canvas.mjs)
choiceFlow.gapReason: the choice flow (Spec 43) holds no setting for this element: build it, map it to a flow setting or record it as a deliberate difference
choiceFlow.reason: a choice flow is the sgs/choice-flow block family (Spec 43 FR-43-1, FR-43-19, FR-43-24, FR-43-26): one sgs/form-step holding an sgs/choice-flow-question per group of options (each option an entry of the question's options), a panel a question opens underneath a step holding its fields and an sgs/choice-flow-result, the add-to-bag control a result step, and the summary, close, skip and continue pieces the flow's own settings; the draft's elements are absorbed into the flow the words the flow holds no setting for are ordinary blocks beside it in its post (the linked flow renders every top-level block, FR-43-6), and only a control none of these holds is a gap row

toggle.reason: a typed glyph in the toggle's icon ring is drawn by the accordion as the Lucide icon of the same shape (lib/skeleton-widgets.mjs::toggleIcon): the closed unit's glyph is the open icon, a different glyph in the open unit's ring the close icon, and the same glyph turned further when open the shape the turn ends on (turns: a plus turned 45 degrees is a cross) as the close icon, so the clone cross-fades the two icons; the turn itself (iconRotation) is a style value no skeleton carries (R-47-10), and the draft's turning transition is the motion route's

childSlots.reason: the accordion keeps its rows' look as its own settings, read on the fixture's open first item and closed second item: which child is open is read from the site look's attributes (pathAttrs: the saved-open item carries open; lib/skeleton-child-slots.mjs::unitSlots), the current child the one headerFontWeight or itemBackgroundOpen reaches in the open state and the resting child one they reach that is not open (with no recorded attributes, the first child each setting's slot names); a closed unit's row, header and icon ring and the open unit's row, answer, title and category line are read at those children's paths (the title and category settings paint every item's text, and calibration lists only the open child's as their own slot, the closed child's as reached) (lib/skeleton-child-slots.mjs::unitSlots), the resting parts first so a setting on both children takes the closed row's value; the current child is saved open, so its paths are read in the open state first (currentState) and an open-state setting there (the open shadow) takes the open unit's value

taughtBy.key: Contact/78, Help/26, Home/245 and Product/118 (handoff records S-59, S-38, S-11 and S-17)

accordion.scope: two or more sibling units (copies of one loop template, or siblings each holding one control) whose every unit holds exactly one control (an element with a click handler, read from the fact record's events) and a panel template inside the unit that renders under an sc-if whose condition reads a state key that control's handler writes (this.setState, followed through the component's own methods; lib/skeleton-widgets.mjs). The units' parent is the accordion when it holds nothing else, else the run is one accordion with no draft element of its own beside the parent's other children; each unit is an item whose title is the control's largest declared text and whose category is its other text, shown over the title (categoryShown on the item, categoryAlways on the accordion, which has no filter); the control and its glyph are absorbed, the glyph read as the accordion's toggle icon (toggle); a closed item's panel content is read from the loop's data in the draft's logic. A keyed map of open items lets several open; the one item shown open at rest is the one open by default. Not an accordion: a run inside a nav, units whose panels hold only links (a navigation disclosure), a control whose panel is outside its unit (a drawer, modal, form step or show-more opener), chips with no panel (an option picker or filter) and a single toggle. The handoff record of kind accordion is a cross-check: agreement is named in the reason, and a record shown on the surface with no mechanism is a proposal problem
accordion.reason: a run of disclosure units, each a control that opens its own panel, is the accordion (2026-11-18 clone audit G-1: an accordion is never a static container)

slider.classTrack: a track the controls find by its class with a document query (document.querySelector('.rev-rail').scrollBy) is the slider track as a ref-bound one is

currentItem.reason: a draft that shows one item at a time, picked by an index its controls and timer move (a current-item display, lib/fill-list-items.mjs::currentItems), is a slider showing one slide; Fill writes the slider's visible-slides setting (settings.visible) as 1, where the block's default shows several side by side

taughtBy.key: Home/222 (the review track) with Home/220, Home/221 and Home/235

slider.scope: an element bound to a ref whose block children are all copies of one loop template (two or more), with controls outside it whose click handlers scroll that ref (scrollTo, scrollBy, scrollIntoView or a scrollLeft write, followed through the component's own methods) or write a state key the track's own style reads; a timer doing the same is autoplay (its delay the speed); drag handlers on the track are noted only, the draggable setting being a motion value Fill writes. The slides' item fields are matched to each listed block's child settings by name and role (lib/fill-list-content.mjs::matchFields): the first block whose listed roles are all taken is the slider and draws its slides (Fill writes them from the loop); the controls and the wrappers holding only controls are absorbed. Slides no listed block takes keep their proposal, and the track's row is a missing-features row and a proposal problem naming the blocks with the listed capabilities
slider.reason: a track of slides that controls scroll is a slider: slides holding a quote and an author are the testimonial slider, which draws its own arrows and dots (Bean: a review card in the client's own style is sgs/testimonial-slider; narrowed 2026-11-21 by Bean's ruling that a review section naming a review platform is that platform's review block, rules.reviewPlatform, decided before the slider; a wordless control is drawn by the block, never a button reading "Click Here")

taughtBy.key: tests/skeleton-widgets.test.mjs (no saved inventory of the three clients holds a tab set)

tabs.scope: two or more sibling controls, each writing one state key to its own value without reading it (not a toggle), and exactly one rendered panel outside them under an sc-if comparing that key with a value one control writes; the tabs block is the nearest element holding the controls and that panel and nothing else; each control is a tab labelled with its words, the shown panel's content is its tab's, and the others are empty tabs with a handover. Not tabs: links with a real address (route navigation), a choice that narrows a rendered list (optionSetFilter), chips with a pressed or checked state (optionSet, decided first), and anything on a header, menu, panel, drawer, form or form-step surface (mega-menu panels and form steps have their own rules)
tabs.reason: controls that each choose one panel by one state key are tabs
